name: Cowboy Pork and Beans Biscuit Bake
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified at 527 cal / 25g protein per serving over 5 servings - right on target with no adjustment. Uses ground-pork, bacon, baked-beans and refrigerated-biscuits, all tracked commodities, which makes it one of the cheapest builds in the slice. No ground-pork American casserole in the catalog (the two live ground-pork dishes are Korean and Asian meatball). | HARVEST: Source typo '1 packed refrigerated biscuit dough' (likely 'packet') preserved verbatim.
OVERRIDE Refrigerated Biscuits: WAVE-4: '1 packed refrigerated biscuit dough' = one 8-ct can (462 g), not one 58 g biscuit
intro_html: Chuckwagon food, more or less. Ground pork and bacon browned together, stirred into sweet baked beans, then topped with biscuit dough and baked until the biscuits are golden and the beans are bubbling up around the edges. It is six ingredients, it is loud, and it is the kind of pan that empties fast at a family table. There is nothing sophisticated about it and it does not need to be.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.23. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $26.65 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.90 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $30.93 across 14 servings, roughly $2.21 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $5.49 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $36.42. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost). Canned baked beans are one of the cheapest filling foods in the store, and here they are the base rather than the side.
shop_smart: Canned baked beans by the big can. The large cans run well under the small ones per ounce, and this bake goes through several of them.
Buy ground pork when it is marked down and freeze it flat. It is usually cheaper per pound than ground beef and it brings more flavor to a dish like this one.
Bacon is doing seasoning work. Render it first and cook the ground pork in that fat, and the whole pan tastes smoky without needing an expensive smoked meat.
Refrigerated biscuit dough is the shortcut, but flour and butter are the cheap route. If the cans are not on sale, a quick drop biscuit mixed from pantry staples costs less and bakes the same.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon and render it in a large oven-safe skillet or a wide pot until crisp, then lift it out and leave the fat behind.
Brown the ground pork in that bacon fat over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it goes, until it is cooked through and starting to catch color.
Add the diced onion and cook until soft, then stir in the minced garlic for the last minute.
Pour in the canned baked beans with their sauce, return the bacon, and season with salt and black pepper. Simmer five minutes so everything comes together.
Spread the mixture in a large baking dish and separate the biscuit dough into pieces, laying them across the top with a little space between so they can spread.
Bake at 375F for 25 to 30 minutes until the biscuits are golden through the middle and the beans bubble at the edges.
portion_html: Weigh the finished bake in its dish, subtract the dish weight, divide by 14, and portion to that exact weight so every container gets both beans and biscuit. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, which makes this a very big plate for the money.

head.description: Ground pork and bacon stirred into sweet baked beans and baked under golden biscuits. A 14 serving six ingredient cowboy casserole for cheap meal prep.
head.keywords: cowboy casserole, pork and beans bake, biscuit topped casserole, ground pork recipe, budget meal prep, cheap dinner ideas
steps: Render the chopped bacon, remove it, and keep the fat.
Brown the ground pork in the bacon fat, then soften the onion and garlic.
Stir in the baked beans and the bacon and simmer five minutes.
Spread into a baking dish and lay the biscuit dough across the top.
Bake at 375F for 25 to 30 minutes until the biscuits are golden.
